transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because since I tried to make my art into a real freelance business, I’ve been getting really wound up about invoices and client messages. Then I avoid dealing with them, and it can get to the point where I’m crying at my kitchen table or forgetting basic things, like paying a bill.
Do these feelings seem mainly connected to your freelance art business?
Yes, mostly. It really started when I tried to make my art into an actual freelance business. The invoices and client messages make me so tense that I put them off, and then it snowballs.
Outside of your freelance art business, do you also find yourself feeling this kind of intense anxiety about other parts of your life?
No, not really. It’s mostly tied to the freelance stuff—the invoices and client messages. That’s what gets me worked up and then I avoid it until everything feels overwhelming.
Did these problems start soon after you began trying to make your art a freelance business?
Yes. It was about a month after I took on the community arts contract and started trying to make the business more formal that I began feeling overwhelmed and avoiding things.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I’m not sure I’d call it depressed. I mostly just feel stressed when I have to deal with the business side of things.
Have you had sudden attacks of intense fear or physical panic that come on out of the blue?
No, I haven’t had anything like that come on suddenly out of nowhere.
Has this stress been interfering with your day-to-day functioning?
Yeah, a little. I’ve been putting off replying to a client, and I missed a utility payment while I was trying to keep up with the art display.
Have you been feeling down or sad most days?
I haven’t really noticed feeling sad most days. It’s more that I get stressed when I have to handle the business stuff.
Would you say this has been causing you a lot of distress?

Yeah, I mean, it feels like a lot in those moments. I get really wound up over invoices or client messages, then I avoid them, and sometimes I end up crying at my kitchen table or forgetting things like paying a bill.
Have these stress-related symptoms lasted for more than 6 months?
No, it’s only been about a month—since I started trying to make my art into a more formal freelance business.
Do you feel your reaction to the freelance business stress has been stronger than you would normally expect for the situation?
Yeah, I think so. I know invoices and client messages are normal business stuff, but I get so wound up that I avoid them, and then I end up crying or forgetting basic things like paying a bill.
Has this stress made it hard for you to do your freelance work?
Yeah. I’ve put off replying to a client, and while I was trying to keep up with the art display, I missed a utility payment at home. It’s starting to affect both sides of things.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different parts of your life, not just your freelance art business?
I’m not really sure. I’ve mostly noticed it around the freelance business stuff.
If the freelance business stress were taken away, do you think these symptoms would mostly go away?
I’m not sure, because the contract and all the business changes are still going on. I haven’t really had a period where it was over long enough to know.
In the past month, have you felt sad or down most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not sure I’d say most of the day, nearly every day. It’s more that I feel stressed when I’m dealing with the business stuff.
Over the past month, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I haven’t really noticed that, no. I still enjoy the things I usually do.
Do you feel your reaction to the freelance business stress is stronger than you would normally expect for that situation?

Yeah, I think it probably is. I get really wound up over invoices or client messages, then I put them off until I’m crying at my kitchen table or forgetting regular things, like paying a bill. It feels like more than I should be reacting to it.
Are these feelings mainly happening when you’re dealing with your freelance business?
Mostly, yes. It really kicks up when I have to deal with invoices or client messages for the freelance work. Then I get overwhelmed and avoid it, and it can spiral from there.
Do you also get this same kind of overwhelming anxiety at times when you are not dealing with your freelance business?
Not really. It’s mostly tied to the freelance stuff—when invoices or client messages come up, that’s when I get overwhelmed.
Before you took on the community arts contract, were you having this same kind of anxiety?
No. It started about a month after I took on the community arts contract and started trying to make the business more formal.
